alerts.reason: Reported sales growth slowed from 17.21% year over year in September to 3.98% in December. Fourth-quarter net product sales grew 3.8%, primarily from higher prices (A, D). I forecast growth stays above -5% in March, then falls to -5% or lower in April–June as the benefit from higher prices fades.

Dover's quarterly revenue decline widened from 0.23% to 1.56%. Annual bookings fell 4.4% to $8.0 billion against $8.4 billion of revenue, and volumes fell in several businesses (A, B, D). With orders lagging sales, I forecast a decline under 5% in March and at least 5% in April–June.

Astec's sales fell 3.84% and 3.63% year over year in successive quarters. Backlog fell 37.6% because deliveries outpaced new orders (B, C). I expect remaining orders to keep the March decline under 5%, with fewer orders available to ship in April–June pushing the decline to at least 5%.

Take-Two's revenue decline narrowed from 6.77% in September to 2.95% in December. December net bookings still fell year over year across franchises including NBA 2K and several mobile games (B, E). I forecast the revenue decline stays under 5% in March, then reaches at least 5% in April–June as weaker bookings flow through to revenue.

Cerence accelerated $67.8 million of deferred revenue into December, exceeding the entire $54.6 million year-over-year revenue gain (A, C). That leaves less revenue to recognize later. I forecast March growth remains above -5% and April–June falls to -5% or lower. The timing is uncertain because C does not identify the quarters affected.

Werner's consolidated revenue decline widened from 1.19% to 4.59%. Acquired shipments supported Truckload Logistics revenue even as revenue per shipment fell (B). One-Way Truckload revenue per mile excluding fuel surcharges fell 5.5% (D). I forecast shipment gains keep the March decline under 5%, but continued rate pressure takes the April–June decline to at least 5%.
